interface_decision.semantic_role: properties of a supplied function between operation-bearing group carriers
interface_decision.litex_form: prop is_monoid_hom and prop is_group_hom, followed by named theorem projections and consequences
interface_decision.rejected_nearest_form: a homomorphism struct would duplicate the supplied function even though this slice only classifies and reasons about f

proof_spine: A monoid homomorphism preserves identity and multiplication.
A group homomorphism is the same property specialized to packaged Group operations.
The defining property directly exposes multiplication preservation.
Multiplication preservation plus the group laws proves inverse preservation.

blocks.intent: Define preservation of monoid identity and multiplication for a supplied function.

attempts.candidate:
try:
    prop is_monoid_hom(M, T set, mulM fn(x, y M) M, oneM M, mulT fn(x, y T) T, oneT T, f fn(x M) T):
        f(oneM) = oneT
        forall x, y M:
            f(mulM(x, y)) = mulT(f(x), f(y))

try:
    thm group_hom_map_inv:
        ? forall G, H nonempty_set, source &group::Group<G>, target &group::Group<H>, f fn(x G) H, x G:

            =>:
                f(source.inv(x)) = target.inv(f(x))
        by def $group::group_laws(H, target.mul, target.one, target.inv)
        source.mul(source.inv(x), x) = source.one
        target.mul(f(source.inv(x)), f(x)) = f(source.mul(source.inv(x), x)) = f(source.one) = target.one

        target.mul(target.mul(f(source.inv(x)), f(x)), target.inv(f(x))) = target.mul(target.one, target.inv(f(x))) = target.inv(f(x))
